## Summary

Built and meshed the plane U-bend duct in `/work/20260911-114420-47b5/bash-t1`.

**Geometry realized:** two 120 mm horizontal legs, 10 mm passage width, joined by a 180° bend with 15 mm centreline radius (10 mm inner / 20 mm outer wall radius) — matching the brief exactly.

**Method:** pure `blockMesh` (`system/blockMeshDict`), four hex blocks — two straight legs plus two 90° bend quarters — built the same way OpenFOAM's own `squareBendLiq` tutorial handles a bend, with `arc` edges specified by centre (`origin`). One cell thick in z with `frontAndBack` typed `empty`, the standard OpenFOAM "2D" recipe.

**A dead end worth knowing about:** I first tried the toolbox's gmsh-based `duct2d.py` recipe (quad-recombine + extrude), adapted with circular-arc edges for the bend outline. `checkMesh` reported "Mesh OK" but the cells were **prisms, not hexahedra** — confirmed by reading gmsh's own element-type codes directly rather than trusting the summary label. `checkMesh`'s health check doesn't distinguish cell shape quality this way, so this could easily have gone unnoticed. Switching to `blockMesh` sidestepped the issue entirely and gave a clean structured hex mesh.

**Result:** 2880 hexahedral cells, ~1 mm resolution (10 cells across the passage, 120 along each leg, 24 per 90° bend quarter). `checkMesh`: **Mesh OK** — max non-orthogonality 0.84°, max skewness 0.033, max aspect ratio 1.42 (all excellent). Patches: `inlet`, `outlet` (10 mm² each, at the two open leg ends), `wall` (all solid duct walls), `frontAndBack` (empty).

A render (`look.png`) confirms the shape and patch placement visually — it's in the case directory and mirrored to your screen already.

Only the mesh was requested, so that's as far as I took it: `system/controlDict`/`fvSchemes`/`fvSolution` here are minimal stubs needed only to run `checkMesh`, not a real incompressible case. Setting up an actual solve (choosing `simpleFoam` vs `pimpleFoam`, laminar vs turbulent, and writing `0/U`, `0/p`) would need a flow rate or velocity to size the Reynolds number against — let me know if you want me to proceed with that and what flow condition to target.
